title: CRISPR/Cas12a Multiplex Genome Editing of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and the Creation of Yeast Pixel Art
protocol: Prepare the Cas12a plasmids.
Obtain the pCSN067 plasmid.
Amplify the pCSN067 plasmid to obtain a high amount.
Transform 25 µL of purchased chemically competent E. coli cells with the plasmid pCSN067 according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Dilute the transformation mix 10 times in 2x peptone-yeast (PY).
Dilute the transformation mix 50 times in 2x PY.
Plate out 10x dilutions on 2x PY agar plates containing ampicillin (0.1 g/L).
Incubate the plates overnight at 37 °C.
Pick 2 to 3 colonies and inoculate each colony in 3 mL of 2x PY.
Grow the inoculated cultures overnight at 37 °C in a shaking incubator at 180 rpm.
Purify the plasmid using a plasmid purification kit according to manufacturer's instructions.
Order the single crRNA array for multiplex genome editing experiments as synthetic DNA.
Amplify the ordered single crRNA array using primers KC-101 and KC-102.

Prepare the PCR amplification mix containing: 0.5 µL of DNA polymerase, 10 µL of 5x buffer required for the DNA polymerase, 1 µL of 10 mM dNTPs, 2.5 µL of 10 µM forward primer, 2.5 µL of 10 µM reverse primer, 2 µL of DNA template at a concentration of 5 ng/µL and ultrapure H2O up to a total volume of 50 µL.
Perform the reaction in a thermocycler with an initial denaturation at 98°C for 3 min.
Denature the DNA at 98°C for 10 s.
Hybridize the primers at 60°C for 20 s.
Extend the DNA synthesis at 72°C for 15 s.
Repeat steps (ii) to (iv) 30 times.
Perform a final extension at 72°C for 5 min.
Hold the reaction at 12°C until further analysis.
Analyze the PCR products by electrophoresis on a 0.8% agarose gel run at 5 V/cm for 40 min using a DNA loading dye and DNA ladder.
Purify the PCR products using a PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Obtain the pRN1120 plasmid.
Amplify the pRN1120 plasmid to obtain a high amount.
Transform 25 µL of purchased chemically competent E. coli cells with plasmid pRN1120 according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Dilute the transformation mix 10 times in 2x PY.
Dilute the transformation mix 50 times in 2x PY.
Plate out 10x and 50x dilutions on 2x PY agar plates containing ampicillin (0.1 g/L).
Incubate the plates overnight at 37°C.
Pick 2 to 3 colonies from the plates.
Inoculate each colony in 3 mL of 2x PY.
Grow the inoculated cultures overnight at 37°C in a shaking incubator at 180 rpm.
Purify the plasmid using a plasmid purification kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Linearize plasmid pRN1120 with EcoRI-HF and XhoI.
Prepare a digestion mix composed of 1 µg of pRN1120, 5 µL of 10x buffer, 1 µL of EcoRI-HF, 1 µL of XhoI and ultrapure H2O up to a total volume of 50 µL.
Incubate the digestion mix at 37 °C for 2 h.
Inactivate the reaction at 65 °C for 20 min.
Analyze the linearized plasmid by electrophoresis on an agarose gel (0.8%, 40 min, 5 V/cm).
Include a circular plasmid as a control in the analysis.
Purify the linearized plasmid using a PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Assemble POT expression cassettes via a 4-part assembly using a GGC reaction.
Measure the concentration of DNA parts using a spectrophotometer.
Dilute each DNA part in ultrapure H2O to a final concentration of 15 fmol/µL.
Prepare a reaction mix composed of DNA fragments, buffer, ligase, and water.
Perform the GGC reaction in a thermocycler according to specified program steps.
Transform 25 µL of chemically competent E. coli cells with 3 µL of the GGC reaction mix.
Dilute the transformation mix 10 times and 50 times in 2x PY.
Plate out 10x and 50x dilutions on 2x PY agar plates containing ampicillin.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Pick 2 to 3 colonies from each plate.
Inoculate each colony in 3 mL of 2x PY.
Grow overnight at 37 °C in a shaking incubator at 180 rpm.
Purify the plasmids using a plasmid purification kit according to manufacturer's instructions.
Design primers complementary to the connector sequence present at the start and the end of each expression cassette.
Prepare PCR amplification mixes for each plasmid containing specified components.
Perform the PCR reaction in a thermocycler with specific cycling conditions.
Analyze the PCR products by electrophoresis on a 0.8% agarose gel at 5 V/cm for 40 min using DNA loading dye and DNA ladder.
Purify genomic DNA from wild type S. cerevisiae CEN.PK113-7D29.
Grow the strain in a 500 mL shake flask filled with 100 mL of yeast extract peptone dextrose (YEPD, 2% glucose) medium at 30°C and shaking at 250 rpm for 48 hours.
Centrifuge 2 mL of broth at 16,000 x g for 1 minute to harvest the cells.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells in physiological salt (200 μL; 0.85% NaCl solution) with RNase (10 μL, 10 mg/mL).
Add yeast lytic enzyme (4 µL) to the resuspended cell mixture.
Incubate the cell suspension at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Vortex shortly after adding 300 µL of cell lysis solution.
Vortex vigorously for 20 seconds after adding 168 µL of protein precipitation solution.
Centrifuge at 16,000 x g and 4°C for 10 minutes to separate the protein fraction.
Collect 600 µL of supernatant in a new tube.
Mix with 600 µL of isopropanol and vortex shortly.
Spin down at 16,000 x g at room temperature for 10 minutes to recover DNA.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation and keep the pellet.
Wash the pellet with 200 µL of ethanol (70%).
Centrifuge at 16,000 x g at room temperature for 10 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Incubate the tube at room temperature for 10 minutes with the lid opened to evaporate the ethanol.
If liquid in the tube is still visible, repeat the ethanol washing step.
Do not dry the pellet for longer than 10 minutes to prevent decreased solubility of the DNA.
Dissolve DNA in 50 µL of TE buffer.
Store purified DNA at 4°C.
Design integration flank DNA sequences such that approximately 1000 bp of genomic DNA will be removed upon introduction of donor DNA.
Design forward and reverse primers for the left flanking region to amplify approximately 500 bp of genomic DNA positioned 5’ (left) of the integration site.
Include 20 bp of homology with the intended flanking region in the forward primer for the left flank.
Include 20 bp of homology with the intended flanking region and a desired 50-bp connector sequence in the reverse primer for the left flank to enable in vivo assembly later on.
Design forward and reverse primers for the right flanking region to amplify approximately 500 bp of genomic DNA positioned 3’ (right) of the integration site.
Include 20 bp with homology with the intended flanking region and a desired 50-bp connector sequence in the forward primer for the right flank to enable in vivo assembly later on.
Include 20 bp of homology with the intended flanking region in the reverse primer for the right flank.
Amplify the flanking regions using designed primers (e.g., primers KC-109 to KC-120).
Measure the concentration of purified genomic DNA template for PCR and adjust to 50 ng/µL.

Prepare PCR amplification mixes by combining genomic DNA, forward and reverse primers (each at 10 µM), 1 µL of 10 mM dNTPs, 10 µL of 5x buffer, 0.5 µL of DNA polymerase (1.0 U), and ultrapure H2O to a total volume of 50 µL.
Perform PCRs in a thermocycler with initial denaturation at 98 °C for 3 min.
Continue PCR cycles: 98 °C for 20 s, followed by annealing at 60 °C for 20 s, and extension at 72 °C for 15 s. Repeat this cycle 30 times.
Final extension step: 72 °C for 5 min.
Hold the reaction mixture at 12 °C until further analysis.
Analyze PCR products by electrophoresis on a 0.8% agarose gel at 5 V/cm for 40 min using DNA loading dye and DNA ladder with fragments ranging from 100 to 10,000 bp.
Purify the correct PCR products using a PCR purification kit according to manufacturer instructions.
Prepare 10x TE buffer containing 100 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 10 mM EDTA, total volume of 50 mL.
Prepare 1 M LiAc at pH 7.5, total volume of 50 mL.
Prepare 50% PEG 4000, total volume of 100 mL.
Check that PEG 4000 stock is at pH 5 before use.
Filter-sterilize the prepared stock solutions.
Prepare LiAc-TE solution containing 0.1 M LiAc, 10 mM Tris-HCl, 1 mM EDTA, total volume of 0.5 mL.
Prepare PEG-LiAc-TE solution containing 40% PEG 4000, 0.1 M LiAc, 10 mM Tris-HCl, 1 mM EDTA, total volume of 1 mL.
Use water with a pH higher than 5 for all transformation steps.
Prepare a pre-culture by growing strain CEN.PK113-7D in a 100 mL shake flask containing 20 mL of YEPD (2% glucose) medium and incubate overnight at 30 °C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Measure the OD600 of the pre-culture (ODpc).
Calculate the dilution factor (df) between the volume of pre-culture and the volume of fresh medium required for preparation of the cells.
Calculate the volume of the pre-culture (Vi) required for inoculation based on the dilution factor.
Prepare the transformation culture by inoculating 20 mL of YEPD with the calculated volume of pre-culture.
Incubate at 30 °C with shaking at 250 rpm until an OD600 of 1.0 is reached.
Harvest cells by centrifuging the broth at 2,500 x g for 5 min and discarding the supernatant.
Wash the cells in 20 mL of room temperature demineralized water.
Repeat the centrifugation step to keep the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 100 μL of LiAc-TE solution.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 5 µL of single-stranded carrier DNA (10 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA) and mix by pipetting.
Pipette 1 μg of plasmid pCSN067 into the microcentrifuge tube.
Add 600 µL of PEG-LiAc-TE solution and mix by pipetting.
Incubate for 30 min at 30 °C while shaking at 450 rpm in a table top heat block.
Add 70 µL of DMSO (100%) to the transformation mixture and mix by pipetting.
Perform heat-shock by incubating the transformation mixture at 42 °C for 15 minutes in a water bath.
Recover the cells by transferring the mixture to a 15 mL round bottom tube.
Add 10 mL of YEPD (2% glucose) to the tube.
Incubate overnight at 30 °C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Centrifuge the transformation mix at 2,500 x g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in approximately 200 µL of the remaining solution.
Plate out 150 µL of the transformation mix on YEPD (2% glucose) agar plates supplemented with 0.2 g/L G418.
Plate out a 20x dilution of the transformation mix in YEPD (2% glucose) of transformation mix on YEPD (2% glucose) agar plates supplemented with 0.2 g/L G418.
Incubate the plates at 30 °C for 48 – 72 hours.
Pick a single transformant and re-streak on a YEPD (2% glucose) agar plate supplemented with 0.2 g/L G418 to obtain single colonies.
Prepare a pre-culture by growing the strain pre-expressing Cas12a in a 100 mL shake flask containing 20 mL of YEPD medium supplemented with 0.2 g/L G418.
Incubate overnight at 30 °C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Pipette 1 µg of the single crRNA array into a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 µg of the linearized recipient plasmid for the crRNA array to the microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 µg of donor DNA to the microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 µg of each flanking region to the microcentrifuge tube.
Prepare negative control using ultrapure H2O.
Determine transformation efficiency using positive control (1 µg circular pRN1120).
Verify CRISPR editing introduction of donor DNA using appropriate controls.
Check if donor DNA can be integrated outside of target with specific controls.
Confirm full linearization of pRN1120 with designated controls.
Plate out 150 μL transformation mix and a 20x dilution on YEPD agar supplemented with G418 and NTC.
Incubate plates at 30 °C for 48 – 72 hours.
Pick single colored transformant from the plate.
Re-streak picked colonies on YEPD agar to obtain single colored colonies.
Count number of colored and white colonies on transformation plates.
Re-streak a colored single colony from a transformation plate on a YEPD (2% glucose) agar plate without G418 and NTC selection.
Incubate the re-streaked plate for 48 hours at 30 °C.
Pick a single colony from the incubated plate.
Inoculate a 500 mL shake flask filled with 100 mL of YEPD (2% glucose) medium with the picked colony.
Incubate the inoculated medium for 48 hours at 30 °C and shaking at 250 rpm.
Isolate the genomic DNA from the cultured yeast as described in Section 4.1.
Design primers which anneal to genomic DNA outside of the transformed flanking regions and the gene of interest.
Amplify region of interest as described in Section 4.4.2.
Adjust the time of the extension step in PCR according to the length of the template and manufacturer’s recommendations for the DNA polymerase.
Prepare a picture template for the yeast pixel art.
Resize the original RGB picture (220 × 280 pixels) to create a final 64 × 96 pixels grey-scale image.
Convert the RGB picture into grey-scale using the formula provided.
Develop an ImageJ plugin applying the given rules to categorize the pixels.
Inoculate 500 mL shake flasks containing 100 mL of YEPD medium with three differently colored carotenoid-producing S. cerevisiae strains and wild type CEN.PK113-7D.
Incubate cultures overnight at 30 °C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Transfer 0.5 mL of the overnight culture to a tube filled with 0.5 mL of sterile non-ionic density gradient medium.
Mix by vortexing briefly.
Transfer the cell suspension to a qualified reservoir, 2 x 3 well.
Spot cells using an acoustic liquid handler instrument from a qualified reservoir source plate onto a microplate containing 50 μL of YEPD (2% glucose) agar.
Define wells on the plate as a 64 × 96 grid.
Spot 25 nL of each S. cerevisiae strain from the 2x 3 well reservoir source plate using a .csv file with the fluid calibration setting 6RES_AQ_GPSA2 onto the destination microplate.
Define each 25 nL droplet as a pixel in the 64 x 96 grid translated to well positions (e.g., A01, B01, C01).
Incubate the microplate at 30 °C for 48 hours.
Store the agar plate at 4 °C for at least 72 hours to intensify the colors of the strains.
